decision_scope: Board decision support for PAIGE conversion layout A vs B

basis: industrial benchmark from corrugated plant report
Factory Graph contract and simulation hypotheses
economic penalties for production loss, starvation, downtime and energy inefficiency
assumptions: Equipment is equivalent between models; layout is the differentiating factor
The production volume is high enough for WIP and flow stability to materially affect output
Operational loss has monetary consequence as output is lost, service slips, and energy increases

model_b.strategic_label: higher resilience and better flow stability

base_case.comment: Model B produces 6-12% more usable output than A in normal operation.

peak_demand_case.comment: Under +20% demand, A loses 8-15% of reachable output and B loses 3-7%.

high_mix_case.comment: In high-mix production with frequent changeovers, A suffers a stronger OEE drop.

supply_interruption_case.comment: Model B absorbs short interruptions better due to the second WIP buffer.

economic_model.decision_summary: Model B is preferred when the project can absorb higher capex, because it generates greater operational value, better output continuity and stronger protection against flow disruptions.

board_recommendation.reason: The operational and economic penalties of Model A outweigh its initial simplicity for realistic mixed-demand corrugated production.
